jobs.title: Senior / Principal Power Systems Engineer
jobs.excerpt: Reporting to the Director of Power Systems Modeling, you will serve as the primary Subject Matter Expert (SME) for transmission planning and generation interconnection.
jobs.description:
Reporting to the Director of Power Systems Modeling, you will serve as the primary Subject Matter Expert (SME) for transmission planning and generation interconnection. This is a high-impact technical role where your deep understanding of power systems will not only drive complex study work but also serve as the "blueprint" for our software development team. You are the bridge between traditional electrical engineering and modern digital transformation. You are also expected to contribute towards the successful completion of a range of consulting projects focused on power system planning studies involving Steady-State, Short Circuit, Transient Stability, Generator and Renewables Interconnections, Large Loads and Data Centers, Electromagnetic Transients (EMT), Model Quality Tests (MQT) and benchmarking, Power System Economics, Market Analysis, and Grid Resilience.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Execute Complex Power System Studies: Lead and perform advanced transmission planning and generation interconnection studies (System Impact, Feasibility, and Deliverability) across multiple North American markets (WECC, PJM, MISO, ERCOT, SPP, SERC, etc.).
  • Technical Authority on Interconnection: Act as the lead expert for both large-scale generation (including IBR) and large-load interconnection requests, navigating the specific tariff and reliability requirements of various RTOs/ISOs.
  • Product Strategy & SME Support: Collaborate directly with our software engineers to translate complex engineering workflows into automated tools. You will define the logic, "teach" the software team the engineering nuances, and validate the output of our internal automation frameworks.
  • Advanced Modeling: Build, tune, and validate high-quality power system models for steady-state, short circuit, transient stability, and EMT analyses using industry-standard tools.
  • Automation Mindset: While we have dedicated software developers, you will be expected to use Python and SQL to automate your own workflows and prototype new ideas that can be scaled into production-level software.
  • Support Business Growth: Collaborate with the leadership team to develop and implement strategies for expanding our consulting services, including identifying emerging needs and new market opportunities and service offerings.
  • Engage with Stakeholders: Build and maintain strong relationships with internal and external stakeholders, including utilities, RTOs, project developers, and regulatory bodies, to advocate for and advance Simple Thread’s projects.
  • Innovate and Improve: Lead the development of innovative methodologies and tools that enhance power systems analysis and streamline processes for both internal and client use.
  • Mentor and Lead: Guide and instruct team members using a strong technical understanding of generation (including IBR), transmission, interconnection, customer and load, and modeling principles.
Regulatory Compliance: Ensure all study work and automated processes adhere strictly to NERC and regional reliability standards.

Qualifications

  • Education: Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering with a focus on Power Systems; a Master’s or PhD degree is highly preferred.
  • Experience: Minimum of 8 years of experience in transmission planning, interconnection studies, EMT analyses likely gained within a utility, RTO, or specialized consulting firm.
  • Market Versatility: Proven track record of navigating the study processes and TARA/PSSE/PSCAD modules for multiple regions (e.g. ERCOT MQT, PJM GD, MISO RIST, CAISO GD, etc.).
  • Tool Proficiency: Expert-level command of PSSE, TARA, PSLF, PSCAD, EMTP, and PowerWorld.
  • Coding Literacy: Proficiency in Python is required for workflow automation. While you don't need to be a full-stack developer, you must be comfortable reading/writing scripts and eager to work in a software-centric environment.
  • Load & Generation Expertise: Deep knowledge of both traditional generation and the unique challenges of Inverter-Based Resources (IBR) and large industrial load and data centers integration.
  • Communication: The ability to distill highly technical engineering concepts into clear requirements for software developers and actionable insights for clients.

Nice-to-Have Qualifications

  • Experience with PowerGEM TARA’s automation API.
  • Familiarity with Git or other version control systems.
  • Experience with EM/ES interferences, grounding (GPR, step & touch) analysis using CDEGS,
  • Familiarity with arc flash analysis using ETAP

Join Us:

Simple Thread offers an opportunity to be at the forefront of technological innovation in the energy industry. We are looking for someone who shares our passion for making a difference and is ready to tackle the challenges of integrating software solutions with energy systems. If you’re passionate about power systems, driven by growth, and eager to make an impact, we want to hear from you.

What We Offer

A Great Team – Our team is the best part of working here. We only hire people who are fantastic teammates – competent and smart, sure, but also humble, positive, and generous.

Great Clients – We work with mostly small and medium clients, for whom our projects make a huge impact. We prioritize clients who are pleasant and good to work with, people who share our values of transparency and empathy.

Work From Home – We are a distributed company. Everyone works from home.

Flexible Work Schedule – We require a certain amount of overlap with the rest of the team, but if you have a predictable schedule, we can probably support it, e.g., ending at 3:30 every day or being out every Friday morning.

Good Work Life Balance (really) – We ask our team to work 40 hours a week*. That’s all: a good, productive 40 hours. And then we try our best to leave you alone off the clock. We do this in part because that’s how we want to live but also because we want our team to be recharged and ready to do their best when working. *If you need to work fewer than 40 hours, that might be possible too; let’s talk.

Competitive Compensation – We offer highly competitive salary and benefits, including generous time off, pension plan (401k or RRSP), FSA, medical and dental insurance, support for continuous growth and professional development. We hire remotely and adjust compensation to meet individual needs, but the standard salary range for this role is $145,000 to $225,000, varying highly with individual experience and strengths.

Simple Thread values diversity in all of its forms, and we hire the best person we can for each role, no matter your personal background. Research tells us that applicants who are female or non-binary, as well as applicants who are people of color, are less likely to apply for roles they do not feel 100% qualified for. If you think you meet more than 50% of our requirements but fewer than 100% of them, please apply. We’re imperfect communicators, so think of our job postings as the starting point for discussion rather than proof that you shouldn’t apply.

JOB SUMMARY

One More Child is seeking to employ a full-time Data Analyst to support its mission of impacting vulnerable children and struggling families through the collection, integration, analysis, forecasting, and visualization of organizational data. The Data Analyst will bridge the gap between raw data and actionable intelligence by leveraging Microsoft Fabric's unified analytics platform to transform data into strategic insights that improve decision-making across fundraising, finance, program operations, and organizational leadership.

This position will be responsible for analyzing data from multiple sources, developing semantic data models, identifying trends and opportunities, conducting predictive analysis, and delivering interactive Power BI dashboards that translate data into meaningful business insights. The ideal candidate will possess strong analytical skills, advanced Microsoft Fabric and Power BI expertise, and the ability to communicate complex data findings to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

  • Utilize SQL, Power BI, and Fabric analytics tools to identify insights, opportunities, risks, and performance trends.
  • Develop and support machine learning and predictive models using Microsoft Fabric Data Science tools, Spark and/or Python.

The Home Health and Hospice Coding Specialist is responsible for reviewing clinical documentation and assigning accurate ICD-10-CM diagnosis codes for home health and hospice patients. This role requires strong knowledge of home health and hospice coding guidelines, Medicare Conditions of Participation, LCD/NCD guidance, PDGM requirements, hospice eligibility documentation, and appropriate sequencing of diagnoses.

What You’ll Do In This Role

  • Review home health and hospice clinical documentation across all time points (SOC, ROC, Recertification, Transfer, Discharge, Admission) to assign accurate ICD-10-CM diagnosis codes.

  • Sequence diagnoses in strict compliance with ICD-10-CM guidelines, CMS requirements, PDGM payment methodologies, and hospice coding expectations.

  • Audit clinical charts to identify documentation gaps or inconsistencies, and collaborate with clinical leadership or compliance teams to resolve query needs.

  • Support revenue cycle efficiency by meeting established productivity and turnaround time goals to prevent delays in billing and claim submissions.

  • Assist with internal quality assurance and external medical reviews, including TPE, ADRs, and compliance audits.

  • Collaborate cross-functionally with clinical, QA, compliance, and revenue cycle teams to drive documentation integrity and regulatory readiness.

  • Maintain an advanced, current knowledge base of CMS guidance, Medicare regulations, LCDs, and payer-specific updates.

  • Ensure absolute data privacy and HIPAA compliance when handling all Protected Health Information (PHI).

  • Generate and maintain tracking logs, status updates, and coding reports for management as required.
Core Competencies

  • Professional Communication: Exceptional verbal and written communication skills tailored for cross-functional collaboration with clinical, quality, compliance, and billing teams.

  • Independent Execution: Highly autonomous self-starter capable of managing priorities, meeting tight turnaround times, and executing responsibilities with minimal supervision.

  • Clinical Accuracy: Strong clinical judgment paired with meticulous attention to detail.

  • Risk Management: Proficient in proactive problem identification, timely escalation, and maintaining absolute confidentiality and HIPAA compliance.

The Experience You’ll Bring
Required

  • Experience: 2+ years in Home Health, ICD-10 coding, and OASIS review.

  • Certification: Active HCS-D and HCS-O certifications.

  • Skills: Extensive background in Plan of Care (POC) and HOPE documentation review.

  • Knowledge Base: Comprehensive mastery of PDGM, Medicare CoPs, HHVBP, Star Ratings, and ICD-10 Official Coding Guidelines.

Preferred

  • CHS-C certified

  • Dual-specialty coding experience across both Home Health and Hospice care settings.

  • Direct experience supporting TPE, ADR, medical reviews, and internal/external compliance audits.

  • Proficiency in industry-standard EMRs (e.g., Homecare Homebase, WellSky, MatrixCare, Careficient, Netsmart).

  • Solid understanding of OASIS accuracy, clinical quality measures, hospice documentation integrity, and billing-related coding guidelines.

Compensation
  • Pay per chart : Minimum of six charts per day
    • Coding only: $15 per chart
    • Coding and OASIS/HOPE: $35 - $38 per chart (based on relevant experience)
    • Coding/OASIS/HOPE/POC: $35 - $40 per chart (based on relevant experience)

jobs.title: Helpline Contact Center Supervisor
jobs.excerpt: Health Resources in Action, Inc.  (HRiA) is a non-profit organization working to improve and reimagine public health.
jobs.description:
Health Resources in Action, Inc. (HRiA) is a non-profit organization working to improve and reimagine public health. We connect, consult, and collaborate to solve complex challenges of access and equity in our health and social systems. Together with our partners, clients, and collaborators, we create actionable solutions so that all people can thrive.

In 1957, The Medical Foundation (TMF) was created to primarily fund biomedical research in Massachusetts. Since then, we’ve been on a journey of evolution. We changed our name to Health Resources in Action (HRiA) to reflect our impact in the field of public health. Today, HRiA works with individuals, organizations, and communities to drive a policy and systems change approach to advance health and racial equity.

HRiA seeks sustainable solutions for complex problems using an anti-racist approach. We aim to be adaptable and flexible in meeting clients and partners where they are, offering our decades of knowledge and resources to collectively realize our dream of equitable, sustainable health for all. The foundation of this work is centered on our values:

  • Health and racial equity by identifying and addressing the root causes of health inequities, intentionally working to shift narratives and power imbalances and disrupt all systems of oppression.
  • Leading with heart by demonstrating our passionate commitment to our work, continuously challenging ourselves with humility and vulnerability while pursuing and holding ourselves accountable to our mission.
  • Collaboration by intentionally and respectfully leading, partnering, and following to strengthen relationships, uplift different voices and build trust.
  • Innovation by driving toward new strategies, questioning norms, and continuously learning and evolving to support the needs of our clients and communities.

HRiA offers exciting, engaging, and challenging employment opportunities for facilitators, trainers, researchers, analysts, policy specialists, grant managers, and more. People come to HRiA because of our commitment to advancing health equity and inspiring work; they stay for our wonderful clients, partners, and dedicated and dynamic staff. With our growing portfolio of high-impact work, person-centered policies, and generous benefits, our team continually invests in making HRiA a great place to work. Our diverse staff of over 270 people hail from 30+ states, with a homebase in Boston’s Chinatown neighborhood.

As part of our Public Health Services, HRiA manages an extensive portfolio of behavioral health initiatives, including statewide substance use helplines in Vermont and Oregon and substance use and problem gambling helplines in Massachusetts and Illinois. The Illinois Helpline for Opioids and Other Substances (Illinois Department of Human Services, Division of Substance Use Prevention and Recovery) was launched in 2017, building upon our experience operating the MA Substance Use Helpline (Massachusetts Department of Public Health, Bureau of Substance Addiction Services) for over 23 years. HRiA launched the Vermont Helplink (Vermont Department of Health, Division of Substance Use Programs) in 2019. HRiA began operating the MA Problem Gambling Helpline (Massachusetts Department of Public Health, Office of Problem Gambling Services) in 2020 and the Illinois Problem Gambling Helpline (Illinois Department of Human Services, Division of Substance Use Prevention and Recovery) in 2022. In December 2023, HRiA launched the Oregon Recovery Center Hotline, now the Oregon Hopeline (Oregon Health Authority).

The Helpline contact center is the hub for the Helplines. Screening & Information Specialists (SIS) comprise most of the contact center team and respond to incoming Helpline inquiries. Four Contact Center Supervisors provide Helpline services and provide direct supervision to a portion of the SIS team. Three Masters-level Clinicians supervise a portion of the SIS, implement follow-up services, and provide additional coverage and support. Additional Helpline team members deliver and support program operations, marketing and communication, web management, and data analysis and management, supervision, and leadership. The larger team is overseen by the Managing Director, Behavioral Health.

To learn more about HRiA and our helplines, visit the following:

  • HRiA:
  • IL Problem Gambling Helpline:
  • MA Problem Gambling Helpline:
  • IL Helpline for Opioids and Other Substances:
  • VT Helplink: www.VTHelplink.org
  • MA Substance Use Helpline:
  • Oregon Hopeline:

Opportunity

We are seeking a full-time Helpline Contact Center Supervisor to join our team on the Oregon Recovery Center Hotline (Oregon Hopeline), Massachusetts Substance Use & Problem Gambling Helplines (MA Helpline), the Illinois Helpline for Opioids and Other Substances (IL Helpline), the Illinois Problem Gambling Helpline, and the Vermont Helplink (VT Helplink). This is an exciting opportunity to take on a newly developed position to support substance use treatment access across three states and supervise a diverse team of staff.

Position Description

We are seeking a full-time Helpline Contact Center Supervisor to join our team for the MA Helpines, the IL Helplines, and VT Helplink. We refer to these projects collectively as “the Helplines.” This is an exciting opportunity to support substance use treatment and problem gambling treatment access across three states and supervise a diverse team of staff.

The Contact Center Supervisors are responsible for handling incoming Helpline inquiries and providing supervisory support to the contact center team. A portion of their time is providing scheduled and as-needed Helpline coverage, in addition to our dedicated team of 22 Screening & Information Specialists (SIS). This includes responding to incoming calls, online chats, and SMS text messages from people seeking information about and help with accessing substance use and/or problem gambling services for themselves, a family member or friend, and/or a client. In this capacity, they assess Helpline users’ needs, determine the most appropriate substance use prevention, treatment, and/or recovery support service options, identify available options (through the Helplines’ databases), and refer callers to those services. They provide accurate information, education, support, and referrals in a non-judgmental, respectful, and culturally competent manner.

About half of their time, Contact Center Supervisors provide supervisory support to the SIS team. Each Supervisor acts as a shift supervisor for SIS while they are working. This includes monitoring SIS consumer interactions, consulting with SIS and intervening during difficult interactions, and addressing any urgent issues as well as supporting the social-emotional wellbeing of staff and fostering their skill-building and professional growth. The Contact Center Supervisor will provide on-going training to SIS through periodic in-service trainings on relevant topics and will assist in the onboarding of new SIS.

Each Supervisor also directly supervises up to six SIS team members. This includes providing bi-weekly supervision, processing timesheets, and assisting with schedule coordination. (SIS also receive regular, group-level supervision from one of our Clinicians.) Contact Center Supervisors are responsible for supporting contact center operations, including helping to coordinate a 24/7 coverage schedule, staffing, and technology needs. They are the liaisons between the contact center team and information technology (IT) support. The Contact Center Supervisor will also be called upon to contribute expertise to the development of policies, procedures, protocols, and curricula to support the Helplines, and may be engaged in providing this expertise to other HRiA teams and projects focused on substance use, problem gambling, and/or behavioral health equity.

This is a full-time, remote position with a salary range of $57,000 to $64,000 based on skills and experience. Supervisors will receive training to assess the needs of Helpline users, provide appropriate information and referrals to services, and engage with and motivate Helpline users to follow through on referrals. They will also receive training on Contact Center operations, supervision essentials, and addiction, screening, treatment services, and resources.

Benefits

HRiA offers strong benefits to its employees, including:

  • Competitive salaries
  • Health insurance
  • Retirement plan
  • Flexible summer hours
  • Vacation starting at four weeks
  • 13 paid holidays, and office closure at the end of December

Duties and Responsibilities

Management

  • Coordinate and implement projects related to contact center operations, including technology, equipment, onboarding & training, among others, as assigned.
  • Work with Helpline Management to coordinate Helpline staffing schedules to ensure continuous 24-hour staffing coverage.
  • Serve as liaison between SIS and other project and organizational teams, to ensure appropriate representation and facilitate team integration.
  • Supervise up to six SIS.
  • Participate in on-call rotation.

Project Work

  • Troubleshoot technical contact center issues, and serve as liaison to IT support.
  • Assist with coordination and implementation of onboarding and professional development activities.
  • Assess the needs of Helpline users by telephone, online chat, and SMS texting.
  • Provide appropriate information and referrals to substance use, problem gambling, and/or related services.
  • Engage and motivate Helpline users to follow through on referrals by using active listening and motivational interviewing techniques.
  • Obtain feedback on interactions with Helpline users.
  • Gather and record data from Helpline users in Helpline database.
  • Verify Helpline users’ insurance status, as applicable.
  • Escalate Helpline user interactions to Helpline Managers as needed.
  • Represent the Helpline at outreach events, meetings, and/or presentations as needed.

Thought Leadership

  • Continue to build and develop expertise in substance use disorders, problem gambling, and behavioral health equity.

Description

At Transcom, we are a global customer experience specialist with over 35 000 employees across the globe. We have already successfully deployed cutting-edge CX products, including AI Agents, Voice automations and real-time translation solutions that transform how millions of people experience customer service every day.


Now we are turning that same firepower inwards. We are looking for someone to make 35 000 colleagues measurably better at their jobs by giving each of them access to the right AI support toolset.


Join Transcom as a Workplace AI Enablement Lead


You are not starting from a blank page. Google's AI suite is Transcom's standard and is already deployed across the business, our security, privacy and compliance colleagues have already done the hard work of clearing the way. Pockets of the organisation are already running on this: early adopters who built their own notebooks, teams who rewired how they handle documentation, people who will happily show you a workflow they invented themselves.


What we need now is someone to take that momentum and make it the norm. The proof of concept phase is behind us. This is now about scale and a broader adoption across the company.


You will be the person who sits down with the HR team, a workforce planner or a country manager and shows them the one workflow that gives them back three hours a week, and then builds the network that spreads it without you in the room.


Your audience is deliberately not IT and not developers. It is everyone else. Your success is measured in habits changed, not features demoed.

This role is open to candidates inCroatia ideallybut we will consider candidates based in Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Egypt, Latvia, Lithuania, Macedonia, Serbia, Slovenia, Spain or Tunisia.


You will


  • Own adoption:Take e.g. Gemini Enterprise and Google NotebookLM from "used well by some" to "indispensable to most", and be accountable for a measurable, visible spike in real daily and weekly usage across the business

  • Build the champion network:Our early adopters already exist and are already sharing — informally, generously and without much structure. You will find them, formalise the network, train them and give them the backing of a proper mandate, so they can sell the tools inside their own teams far better than any central function ever could. Adoption cannot be forced top-down — you will make it grow sideways

  • Create virtual teammates:Some teams have already built their own AI assistants and are seeing the benefit. You will make that repeatable — teaching leaders and contributors to configure specialised notebooks, reusable templates and custom instructions for the routine documentation, analysis and onboarding work that eats their week

  • Cut through the noise:Workspace AI ships new features constantly. You will vet them ruthlessly, ignore what is merely clever, and translate what is genuinely useful into plain, non-technical business language

  • Hold the line on safety:You are not inventing our guardrails from scratch — our security, privacy and ethical AI principles are established, and the specialists behind them are engaged and ready to support you. Your job is to make those boundaries land in everyday practice, so people know exactly what they can put into a prompt, and why they still have to check the answer

  • Prove it: Gather the field intelligence from your champions, build on the success stories we already have, and give leadership short, honest updates with the adoption metrics behind them


What's in it for YOU

  • A genuinely rare mandate: a global company that has already made the AI investment and is now serious about the most important part – getting people to actually drive value out of it

  • Visibility. This role touches every function and every geography.

  • The freedom to shape your own approach and actively influence how ways of working evolve across the organization

  • International and inclusive environment, that makes you feel supported, encouraged and welcome from day one

  • A personalized development plan and a dedicated education budget

  • Flexible work schedule and life-work balance


To be successful in this role, the following is needed:

  • A practitioner, not a commentator:real hands-on experience with Gemini Enterprise, Gemini Advanced and NotebookLM, or close equivalents such as Microsoft Copilot, ChatGPT Enterprise or Claude – you use these tools daily, not occasionally

  • Deep working knowledge of a collaboration suite (Google Workspace strongly preferred: Gmail, Docs, Sheets, Slides, Meet)

  • A translator:a proven ability to explain complex AI capability in simple, non-technical language to people who did not ask for a tech lesson

  • A pragmatist: instinctive bias towards workflows that save time over features that impress engineers

  • An influencer without authority: high credibility among peers, and a track record of inspiring, coaching and building networks of advocates without a reporting line to lean on

  • Confidence facilitating live sessions – demos, lunch-and-learns, open Q&A – and the ability to hold a room, including a sceptical one

  • A solid understanding of and genuine respect for enterprise compliance, security and data privacy principles

  • Experience in digital adoption, enablement, product or platform ownership, or a technical/analytical role in a large distributed organisation

  • A degree in Business Administration, Technology Management, Communication or a related field, or equivalent practical experience

  • English verbal and written is required (C1 or higher level)

  • Well-developed communication skills, a team player mentality and a willingness to share ideas and best practice



If you are tired of watching great AI tools go unused, and you would rather change how a global company works than write another strategy deck about it, let's talk.

Apply now with a full CV in English.

Closing date for applications is Wednesday 30th September 2026.

What Life at Transcom is like

At Transcom, we're relentlessly committed. To our clients and each other. Every day, someone starts their journey with Transcom. Taking the potential they have today and turning it into skills for the future. Getting recognized for working hard, being a team player, and supporting others. Championing positive, lasting change in their teams and communities. That's just how we are at Transcom. Here we care and root for each other. You're included, just as you are, from day one. And with the right mindset, there's no end to how far we can go together.

jobs.description:
PHILANTHROPY OFFICER

Department: Development

PLEASE NOTE: This position is open to clients Texas or Ohio.

JOB SUMMARY

The Philanthropy Officer builds and strengthens meaningful, long-term relationships with donors and prospects who have the capacity and affinity to make significant philanthropic investments in One More Child. Reporting to the Senior Director of Philanthropy, this role engages and grows an assigned portfolio within a specific region, engaging donors through discovery, meaningful engagement, cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship. The Philanthropy Officer develops individualized engagement strategies, builds a healthy pipeline of qualified prospects, and secures annual, capital, endowment, Comprehensive Campaign, and other strategic commitments in alignment with donor interests and One More Child’s priorities. Working collaboratively with the Executive Director of Philanthropy, Chief Advancement Officer and other organizational leaders, the Philanthropy Officer serves as a trusted ambassador for One More Child and invites donors into meaningful participation in the organization’s mission.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND FUNCTIONS

Donor Relationships & Portfolio Management

  • Manage an assigned portfolio of donors, building authentic, long-term relationships through meaningful engagement, discovery, cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship.
  • Develop individualized relationship strategies based on each donor’s interests, passions, capacity, giving history, and relationship with One More Child.
  • Maintain consistent, thoughtful contact with donors through personal visits, calls, meetings, stewardship touchpoints, ministry experiences, events, and other meaningful engagement opportunities.
  • Listen to and understand donor interests and motivations, connecting them with opportunities to meaningfully advance the mission of One More Child.
  • Create meaningful donor experiences in partnership with regional, campus, program, and organizational leaders that deepen understanding of One More Child’s mission and impact.
  • Personally solicit and steward 5- and 6-figure gifts, multi-year commitments, and other philanthropic investments in collaboration with the Executive Director of Philanthropy and organizational leaders.

Prospect & Pipeline Development

  • Identify, engage in discovery, and cultivate prospective donors with the capacity and affinity to make significant investments in One More Child.
  • Build and maintain a healthy portfolio and pipeline, advancing qualified prospects through intentional relationship strategies and appropriate next steps.
  • Participate in regular portfolio and pipeline reviews with the Executive Director of Philanthropy and the Director of Development Strategy, using relationship intelligence to prioritize opportunities and strengthen donor investment.
  • Partner with the Director of Development Strategy to effectively use CRM data, metrics, analytics, and pipeline reporting to inform portfolio management and fundraising strategies.

Strategic & Campaign Fundraising

  • Develop and execute donor strategies that align donor interests and passions with One More Child’s strategic priorities and funding opportunities.
  • Participate in the Comprehensive Campaign and other strategic fundraising initiatives, cultivating and soliciting individual commitments for capital, endowment, annual giving, and other organizational priorities.
  • Collaborate with the Executive Director of Philanthropy, Chief Advancement Officer, Senior Vice President of Strategic Development, and other organizational leaders on significant donor strategies and solicitations.

Donor Communications & Collaboration

  • Provide donor insight and strategic direction for proposals, presentations, stewardship communications, and other materials supporting cultivation and solicitation.
  • Partner with the Director of Development Communications to develop compelling, donor-centered proposals and communications that connect donor interests with meaningful philanthropic opportunities.
  • Collaborate with Advancement, Communications, Programs, Partnerships, regional, and campus teams to ensure a coordinated and compelling donor experience.
  • Serve as an ambassador for One More Child, clearly and authentically communicating its mission, impact, vision, and opportunities for philanthropic partnership through events, personal visits, and speaking opportunities.

Performance & Professional Development

  • Meet established fundraising, portfolio, meaningful engagement, and pipeline goals while maintaining a focus on long-term donor relationships and sustainable philanthropic growth.
  • Maintain accurate and timely records of donor interactions, strategies, next steps, and portfolio activity in the organization’s CRM.
  • Continuously develop knowledge of One More Child’s programs, impact, strategic priorities, and funding opportunities to effectively engage and inspire donors.
  • Demonstrate integrity, discretion, professionalism, initiative, sound judgment, and commitment to ethical, relationship-based philanthropy.
  • Stay current with best practices in philanthropy and continually strengthen skills in donor engagement, discovery, cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship.
  • Travel within assigned region regularly; at least annual visit to Headquarters in Lakeland.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Professional & Organizational Expectations

  • Pursues ongoing personal and professional growth to strengthen expertise and effectiveness in writing, proposal development, project management, and related areas through seminars, webinars, workshops, books, software, professional publications, and professional affiliations.
  • Brings creativity, initiative, strong organizational skills, and a high level of motivation to the role.
  • Demonstrates integrity, sound judgment, and maturity consistent with the organization’s core beliefs and values.
  • Demonstrates a positive attitude and genuine passion for the organization’s mission of providing Christ-centered services to children and families in need.
  • Performs other duties as assigned.

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES

  • N/A


REQUIRED EXPERIENCE AND QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor’s degree in nonprofit management, business, communications, marketing, public relations, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.
  • Minimum of 3–5 years of experience in philanthropy, fundraising, development, sales, relationship management, or a related field.
  • Demonstrated ability to build and maintain authentic, trust-based relationships with individuals and organizations.
  • Experience cultivating relationships and securing financial support, investments, or other commitments from donors, customers, clients, or partners.
  • Strong interpersonal and communication skills, including the ability to listen effectively, ask thoughtful questions, understand motivations, and communicate compellingly with diverse audiences.
  • Ability to develop and execute individualized relationship strategies and manage multiple relationships, priorities, and opportunities with strong organization and follow-through.
  • Demonstrated initiative, sound judgment, professionalism, integrity, and discretion in working with individuals and confidential information.
  • Ability to work collaboratively with organizational leaders, colleagues, and cross-functional teams to advance shared goals.
  • Commitment to the mission, values, and Christian identity of One More Child.
  • Willingness and ability to travel regularly in assigned region for donor visits, meetings, ministry experiences, events, and other relationship-building activities.

PREFERRED EXPERIENCE AND QUALIFICATIONS

  • Demonstrated experience in major gifts, individual philanthropy, or relationship-based fundraising, preferably within a nonprofit or ministry environment.
  • Proven success personally cultivating, soliciting, and stewarding significant individual gifts, including multi-year commitments.
  • Experience securing six-figure or transformational gifts.
  • Experience participating in a Comprehensive, capital, or endowment campaign.
  • Established relationships within the philanthropic community, particularly within the assigned geographic region.
  • Experience managing a donor portfolio and using a CRM to track donor relationships, engagement, strategies, and next steps.
  • Experience using fundraising metrics, analytics, and pipeline information to inform donor strategies and prioritize opportunities.
  • Familiarity with relationship-based fundraising principles centered on discovery, meaningful engagement, and donor-centered philanthropy.

COMPETENCIES

  • Present oneself, both at and outside of work, in a manner keeping with One More Child’s Core Values of Humble, Hungry, Wise, and Called.
  • Relational Intelligence – Builds authentic, trust-based relationships by listening deeply, demonstrating genuine curiosity, understanding donor motivations, and creating meaningful connections.
  • Donor-Centered Philanthropy – Approaches fundraising as an opportunity to understand donor interests and passions and connect them with meaningful opportunities to advance the mission, rather than as a transactional exchange.
  • Strategic Thinking – Develops thoughtful relationship strategies, recognizes opportunities, prioritizes effectively, and balances long-term relationship building with measurable fundraising results.
  • Communication & Influence – Communicates with clarity, confidence, authenticity, and empathy; effectively articulates One More Child’s mission, impact, and philanthropic opportunities and inspires others to engage.
  • Initiative & Execution – Takes ownership, follows through consistently, manages competing priorities effectively, and turns relationship strategies and opportunities into meaningful action and results.
  • Collaboration & Stewardship – Builds strong partnerships with colleagues and organizational leaders, represents One More Child with professionalism and integrity, and demonstrates exceptional care in stewarding donor relationships and resources.

SPIRITUAL QUALIFICATIONS

  • It is the mission of One More Child to provide Christ-centered services to vulnerable children and struggling families. As stated in the Second Amended and Restated Articles of Incorporation, One More Child provides these services in a Christian context consistent with The Baptist Faith and Message (2000). Employees of One More Child commit to live in a manner that is not contrary to this foundational statement of faith.
  • Have had a personal conversion experience with Jesus Christ and been scripturally baptized.
  • Possess a sense of commitment to ministry through vocation.
  • Hold a sincere desire to seek God and His kingdom.
  • Demonstrate personal and devotional habits and practices such as Bible study, prayer, and daily meditation.
  • Be a member of a New Testament, evangelical church in the local community and attend regularly.
  • Engage in witness activities as a normal part of life.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS

These physical requirements are not exhaustive, and One More Child may add additional job-related physical demands to these if the need arises. Corrective devices may be used to meet these physical requirements.

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to sit and talk or hear. The employee frequently is required to use hands to finger, handle, or feel. The employee is occasionally required to walk and reach with hands and arms. The employee must be able to operate a forklift. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision.

This job requires the ability to work in stressful conditions from time to time and remain focused for extended periods of time. The ability to lift up to 50 pounds (boxes, documents, and/or equipment) may be required on occasion.

WORK ENVIRONMENT

The work environment describes the conditions that an employee may encounter when performing their job duties, including but not limited to, the essential functions of the position. Reasonable accommodation may be available to enable individuals with disabilities to perform these duties.

Job functions are performed in a normal office environment, with the option of hybrid/remote. Regular travel within assigned region and one to two visits per year to the headquarters in Lakeland are expected.

DISCLAIMER

This job description is not intended to be an all-inclusive list of the requirements of this position, but to describe the general nature of the job and provide a reasonable representation of its activities. Additional related work may be identified and assigned by the organization and included as an area of responsibility while assessing performance.

EQUAL EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITY STATEMENT

One More Child is committed to a workplace environment that encourages growth and respect for all current and prospective employees based upon job-related factors such as their educational background, work experience, and ability to perform the essential functions of a particular job. It is the policy and practice of One More Child to prohibit any form of discrimination or harassment based on statuses protected under federal, state, or local laws which are applicable to the organization. As a religious organization, One More Child provides services in a Christian context consistent with The Baptist Faith and Message (2000). Employees of One More Child commit to live in a manner that is not contrary to this foundational statement of faith.

You'll build trusted relationships with managers, helping them navigate employee relations matters, organisational change, workforce planning and performance, whilst ensuring an exceptional employee experience.
This is a varied, fast-paced role requiring someone who is comfortable working in ambiguity, balancing operational priorities with longer-term people initiatives, and providing practical solutions to complex people challenges.

Culture and Communications

  • Arrange and attend internal events, communications and training to evangelise our core values and desired culture, keeping them at the forefront of our people’s minds.
  • Identify and implement improvements for diversity and inclusion, health and happiness, work environment, recognition and communication.
  • Challenge behaviours which are not consistent with our people strategy and culture.

Performance Management and Continuous Improvement

  • Identify improvements for departments and individuals by analysing data and other inputs.
  • Assist our leaders in succession planning to solve single points of failure and to plan internal promotions.
  • Provide comprehensive, pragmatic and commercially focused employment advice and best practice guidance to managers, ensuring they are equipped to confidently manage their teams.
  • Coach managers and our people to improve performance and conduct, implementing formal action where required.
  • Act as a trusted advisor on employee relations matters, including disciplinary, grievance, capability, absence management and performance cases.
  • Support organisational change initiatives, restructures and TUPE consultations where required.
  • Support managers in ensuring our people have clear and measurable objectives and development plans.

  • Support the delivery of the People Agenda by working alongside the Head of People and Culture to execute objectives that support the wider priorities of the People Function.
  • Promote fairness, consistency and an excellent employee experience at every opportunity.

  • Coach and advise managers to set meaningful development objectives for their teams and individuals.
  • Implement training sessions and development programmes that inspire our people to do their best work.

jobs.title: Senior AI Software Developer
jobs.excerpt: Over StaxxerStaxxer helpt e-commerce ondernemers hun financiële administratie en compliance te automatiseren.
jobs.description:
Over Staxxer

Staxxer helpt e-commerce ondernemers hun financiële administratie en compliance te automatiseren. Van btw en OSS tot EPR en boekhouding. Wat begon als een dienstverlening voor online verkopers, groeit uit tot een softwareplatform dat e-commerce ondernemers steeds meer financieel werk uit handen neemt.

Daarvoor maken we een belangrijke transitie: van een servicegedreven organisatie naar een softwaregedreven bedrijf. We bouwen verder op onze bestaande producten, data en financiële expertise, met AI als belangrijke versneller.

Een van onze volgende stappen is bijvoorbeeld de ontwikkeling van een E-commerce CFO: een financiële co-pilot die ondernemers niet alleen vertelt hoe ze ervoor staan, maar ook helpt begrijpen waar ze geld verdienen, waar kansen liggen en wat ze kunnen verbeteren.

En daar hebben we jou voor nodig.

Over de rol

We zoeken een Senior AI Software Developer die de brug slaat tussen finance, software en AI.

Je werkt nauw samen met onze financiële experts, product owner en developers. Je ontdekt welke financiële vraagstukken onze klanten dagelijks tegenkomen en vertaalt die naar slimme, schaalbare software.

Je bent geen developer die alleen tickets afwerkt. Je bent een ervaren engineer die problemen begrijpt, technische oplossingen bedenkt en deze zelfstandig realiseert.

In het begin werk je dicht met onze eigen financiële experts. Je bouwt tools waarmee zij sneller en slimmer kunnen werken. Je experimenteert met klanten, valideert oplossingen en ontdekt wat écht waarde toevoegt.

Je krijgt daarin veel vrijheid en verantwoordelijkheid. We zoeken iemand die liever binnen een week een werkende oplossing laat zien dan maanden besteedt aan het schrijven van specificaties.

Wat ga je doen?

1. Financiële advies vertalen naar een AI gedreven software product.

Onze financiële experts helpen dagelijks e-commerce ondernemers met complexe financiële vraagstukken. Jij onderzoekt welke kennis, analyses en werkzaamheden we kunnen automatiseren.

  • Bouw financiële rapportages, analyses, exports en interne tools die gebruikt worden om de e-commerce klant te kunnen voorzien van financiële expertise.

  • Vertaal terugkerende klantvragen naar herbruikbare software.

  • Automatiseer handmatige financiële processen.

2. AI-native producten ontwikkelen

AI verandert fundamenteel hoe financiële software wordt gebouwd en gebruikt. Jij helpt ons die mogelijkheden concreet te maken.

  • Ontwikkel AI-functionaliteiten die ondernemers helpen hun financiële cijfers in te zien, te begrijpen en afwijkingen pro actief te signaleren.

  • Bouw verder op de bestaande AI-assistent binnen My Staxxer.

  • Breid onze MCP-integratie uit, zodat AI-assistenten veilig met financiële klantdata kunnen gaan werken.

  • Experimenteer met LLM’s, agents en bestaande AI-tooling.

  • Zorg dat AI-oplossingen betrouwbaar, controleerbaar en veilig zijn.

3. De E-commerce CFO vormgeven

We weten waar we naartoe willen, maar nog niet precies hoe het eindproduct eruitziet. Dat gaan we ontdekken door te bouwen.

  • Ontwikkel prototypes en MVP’s voor een “e-commerce CFO”, wat een agentic laag is boven onze grote e-commerce data set.

  • Test oplossingen met onze eigen experts en bestaande klanten.

  • Help bepalen welke functionaliteiten voldoende waarde leveren om voor te betalen.

  • Vertaal succesvolle experimenten naar schaalbare productfunctionaliteiten.

Je bouwt dus niet alleen software. Je denkt actief mee over wat we moeten bouwen, waarom en voor wie.

4. Slim bouwen op bestaande technologie

Staxxer heeft al een uitgebreid platform met modules voor btw, OSS, EPR, integraties en boekhouding.

Die bestaande infrastructuur biedt veel mogelijkheden, maar kent ook technische uitdagingen.

  • Ontsluit bestaande data via betrouwbare interfaces en API’s.

  • Bepaal welke data geschikt is voor financiële analyses en AI-toepassingen.

  • Maak pragmatische keuzes tussen hergebruik, refactoring en nieuwbouw.

  • Werk samen met ons development team aan een schaalbare architectuur.

  • Zorg dat nieuwe oplossingen aansluiten op ons bestaande platform.

Je begrijpt dat snelheid belangrijk is, maar dat betrouwbare financiële data niet onderhandelbaar is.

Wat krijg je van ons?

Bij Staxxer krijg je de vrijheid om te bouwen, te experimenteren en daadwerkelijk impact te maken. We bieden je veel verantwoordelijkheid, vertrouwen en de middelen om je werk goed te doen.

  • Een salaris van €5.500 tot €8.000 bruto per maand, op basis van 40 uur en afhankelijk van je ervaring en expertise.

  • Onbeperkte vakantiedagen. We vertrouwen erop dat je zelf een gezonde balans vindt tussen werk en privé.

  • Remote werken. Werk waar je het beste presteert. We verwachten wel dat je aanwezig bent op belangrijke momenten, zoals onze company trips, teamdagen en kerstviering.

  • €100 per maand vrij besteedbaar pensioenbudget. Je bepaalt zelf hoe je dit inzet voor je pensioenopbouw.

  • Een MacBook van de zaak. Inclusief alle software en AI-tools die je nodig hebt.

  • Ruimte voor persoonlijke ontwikkeling. Budget en mogelijkheden voor opleidingen, conferenties en nieuwe technologieën.

  • Veel vrijheid en eigenaarschap. Je krijgt de ruimte om technische keuzes te maken en actief richting te geven aan een nieuwe productlijn.

  • Directe samenwerking met de oprichters. Korte lijnen met ons development team, onze financiële experts en het management.

  • Een ambitieus en gezellig team. Met company trips, teamactiviteiten en momenten om samen successen te vieren.

Waarom Staxxer?

Bij veel bedrijven werk je aan een klein onderdeel van een bestaand product. Bij Staxxer krijg je de kans om vanaf het begin mee te bouwen aan een compleet nieuwe productlijn.

Je hoeft niet vanaf nul te beginnen. We hebben bestaande klanten, financiële experts, een development team en een groeiende hoeveelheid relevante data.

Tegelijkertijd staat de ontwikkeling van onze financiële co-pilot nog aan het begin. Dat betekent veel ruimte om te experimenteren, keuzes te maken en daadwerkelijk invloed uit te oefenen op het eindproduct.

We geloven in kleine teams, veel eigenaarschap en snel leren door dingen daadwerkelijk te bouwen.

Requirements

Wie zoeken we?

We zoeken een ervaren, zelfstandige engineer die energie krijgt van het ontwikkelen van nieuwe producten. Iemand die niet alleen technisch sterk is, maar ook begrijpt hoe je technologie inzet om echte klantproblemen op te lossen.

Wat je meebrengt:

  • Minimaal 5 jaar relevante ervaring in softwareontwikkeling, bij voorkeur binnen een fintech organisatie.

  • Sterke programmeervaardigheden, bijvoorbeeld in Python, TypeScript of PHP, en uitgebreide ervaring met SQL .

  • Ervaring met softwarearchitectuur en het ontwikkelen van betrouwbare, schaalbare applicaties.

  • Je werkt AI-native en gebruikt tools zoals Claude Code, Cursor of vergelijkbare oplossingen dagelijks om sneller en beter software te ontwikkelen.

  • Je hebt ervaring met het zelfstandig ontwikkelen van nieuwe functionaliteiten, van eerste prototype tot productie.

  • Je begrijpt hoe je nieuwe software bouwt op een bestaande codebase met technical debt.

Overview

Who We Are

Because health is personal. That's why Personify Health created the first and only personalized health platform—bringing health plan administration, holistic wellbeing solutions, and comprehensive care navigation together in one place. We serve employers, health plans, and health systems with data-driven solutions that reduce costs while actually improving health outcomes. Together, our team is on a mission to empower people to lead healthier lives.

Learn even more about the work that drives us at personifyhealth.com.

Responsibilities

Utilization Management Nurse (LPN/LVN), Level I

Ready to make sure every member gets the right care at the right time?

Why This Role Matters

Behind every prior authorization and inpatient stay is a member waiting on a decision, and you’re the one who makes sure that decision is timely, accurate, and grounded in evidence. As a Level I Utilization Management Nurse, you review requests for medical necessity, level of care, and benefit coverage, then apply clinical guidelines and plan policies to keep care appropriate and compliant. Your sharp review work protects members from delays and unnecessary services, supports providers who need clear answers, and keeps our programs ready for URAC and NCQA scrutiny. When your reviews are thorough, well-documented, and delivered on time, our whole organization earns the trust of the members and sponsors who rely on us.

What You’ll Actually Do

  • Perform clinical reviews that drive sound determinations: Evaluate requests for medical necessity, appropriate level of care, documentation completeness, and benefit coverage, so members get timely decisions that meet compliance standards.
  • Deliver first-level review across care settings: Review outpatient and ancillary pre-certification and prior authorization requests, inpatient stays (including behavioral health, substance use, skilled nursing, and rehabilitation), and post-service or post-claim reviews as assigned.
  • Apply guidelines in the right hierarchy: Use internal medical policies, group-specific policies, NCCN, and MCG as applicable, and record your criteria and policy rationale in the UM system so every decision stands on solid ground.
  • Escalate the cases that need advanced eyes: Refer requests that fall outside guidelines, fail to meet criteria, or may require adverse determination to senior staff or the Medical Director, and support IRO referrals in line with policy and jurisdictional requirements.
  • Verify benefits and guide members in-network: Review plan documents to support benefit determinations, and redirect providers and members to PPO or in-network options when it fits plan requirements.
  • Build audit-ready case summaries: Prepare clear, complete documentation for Medical Director review, including adverse determination and IRO referral pathways, so every case holds up under scrutiny.
  • Hit productivity, quality, and turnaround targets: Meet established standards, take part in quality activities like inter-rater reliability (IRRA), and apply feedback to keep us audit-ready for URAC, NCQA, and other applicable standards.
  • Protect member privacy at every step: Follow HIPAA and minimum-necessary standards, and complete required annual training and testing on time.
  • Cross-train and cover where the team needs you: Step in to support team operations and service-level commitments, and contribute to staff training as appropriate.

Qualifications

What You Bring to Our Team

Education & Experience:

  • Graduate of an accredited nursing program (LVN/LPN)
  • Current, unrestricted U.S. or U.S. territory nursing license (compact license acceptable where applicable)
  • Minimum 1-2 years of recent clinical experience in acute care, med-surg, ICU/ED, or another relevant setting
  • Prior utilization review or utilization management experience preferred

Technical Skills:

  • Ability to interpret medical records and apply evidence-based criteria and plan medical policies
  • Working knowledge of clinical guidelines such as MCG and NCCN, and UM documentation systems
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Word, Excel, Outlook, and Teams, with the ability to learn additional tools as assigned
  • Comfort working across multiple screens and a headset-based phone system, with proficient typing and accurate data entry
  • Ability to use remote-work technology (e.g., VPN) and departmental platforms (e.g., SharePoint/Drives) in line with security policies

Benefits

The Highlights:

  • Competitive base salary and benefits effective day one
  • Comprehensive medical and dental through our own health solutions (yes, we use what we build)
  • Paid Time Off—rest and recharge time is non-negotiable
  • Mental health support, retirement planning, and financial protection
  • Professional development with clear career progression and learning budgets
  • Mission-driven culture where diverse perspectives drive real impact on people's health

Want the full picture? Visit personifyhealthbenefits.com to explore our complete benefits package, wellness programs, and other employee perks.

Compensation: This position offers a base salary range of $25-$30 per hour, depending on location, skills, and experience. You're eligible for our full benefits package starting day one.

Our Commitment: Personify Health is an equal opportunity employer committed to diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging. We cultivate a work environment where differences are celebrated, and employees of all backgrounds are empowered to thrive—because diversity is core to who we are and critical to our work in health and wellbeing.

Description

CapsLock is a global IT marketing company that pioneers unique, scalable customer acquisition solutions for B2C clients. Role overview

We're looking for a Marketing Design Team Lead who is equal parts creative leader, marketer, and AI geek, someone who knows how to achieve business goals through visuals that actually sell.

You will take a team of 3 AI-driven Creative Designers and scale it to 6. The team produces static ad creatives, photorealistic AI visuals for performance campaigns across paid media channels, and source assets for our video production pipeline.

Your job is to build the company's visual creative engine. Whatever the starting point- a brief, a hypothesis, a raw idea - it leaves the team as a creative that performs.

You'll work closely with Creative Producers, Marketers, Copywriters, Media Buyers, and the Video Editing team, and partner with our Generative AI Pipeline Engineer on tooling and workflows.

What you will work on

  • Lead, mentor, and scale a team of 3 to 6 AI-driven Creative Designers - grow people, not just output;
  • Own the production flow: task distribution, capacity planning, and strict QC - production-grade, not demo-grade;
  • Drive creative direction: concepts, hooks, and visual angles that stop the scroll and convert;
  • Generate ideas yourself and push the team beyond safe iterations - informed by visual trends and competitor creatives;
  • Own the creative testing loop: build a database of winners, analyze failures, turn performance data into next iterations;
  • Track new AI models and tools; be the company's go-to expert on what's creatively possible with AI, staying hands-on in the tools;
  • Run regular R&D and build prompt and style libraries that keep quality consistent as the team grows;
  • Stay hands-on: jump into the tools (Figma, Adobe Suite, AI platforms) when needed to unblock the team, take on the most complex creatives, or test new approaches;
  • Partner with the Generative AI Pipeline Engineer to turn the team's creative needs into pipelines, presets, and automation;
  • Work tightly with Creative Producers, Marketers, Media Buyers, and Video Editors: align on strategy, negotiate deadlines, solve bottlenecks.

Requirements

Your must-haves

You don't need to meet every single requirement. If you're excellent in most of these areas and can show shipped work, we'd love to hear from you.

  • 5+ years of Leadership Experience: You have successfully managed creative/design teams in digital marketing. (This is not a role for a senior designer looking for their first management gig);
  • Mature Leader & Problem Solver: You build clear processes, guide your team, gracefully resolve conflicts, remain highly proactive, and stay completely open to new ideas and approaches;
  • Strong Project Manager: You drive every project cleanly to the finish line. You guarantee top-tier quality, maintain absolute order, and hit strict deadlines without excuses;
  • Strong Visual Craft: composition, lighting, color, typography, anatomy. You can articulate exactly why a creative works or doesn't;
  • Design Toolstack: proficiency in Figma and Adobe Creative Suite; comfortable connecting AI outputs with traditional design pipelines;
  • AI Geek: far beyond basic prompting. You track every new model release and can't wait to test how it could level up ad creatives. Hands-on with modern AI image platforms (Figma Weave, Higgsfield, Magnific, Runway, or similar), using them for creating photorealistic visuals. Able to choose the right tool for each task, as well as to catch and fix artifacts.
  • Performance Marketing DNA: solid understanding of static ad creatives (Google, Meta, and other paid channels). You know what stops the scroll, what makes a visual sell, and how creative decisions move CTR, CPA, and conversion rate;
  • Fluency in English - both spoken and written.

Nice to have

  • A strong portfolio showcasing performance marketing creatives and AI-generated photorealistic work - ideally with examples shipped under your leadership and the results they drove;
  • Experience with creatives for high-CPA verticals (home improvement, insurance, health, legal, finance, or similar);
  • Experience creating visuals for North American audiences - you know what looks native to a US consumer;
  • Understanding of how static visuals feed video production pipelines.

What we offer

  • Remote Work - we offer a truly and fully remote environment. You choose where you are the most productive and comfortable to have an impact.
  • Paid vacations - generous paid vacation policy to ensure you have time to recharge.
  • Unlimited Sick Days - we understand that being only human means getting sick or feeling under the weather from time to time, so we guarantee you time off as long as you need to recover and get back on your feet.

Position Summary

We are seeking a detail-oriented and highly organized Purchasing Specialist to support the day-to-day purchasing operations of a company operating in the marine spare parts industry.

The successful candidate will be responsible for processing requests for quotations (RFQs), sourcing spare parts and materials, coordinating with suppliers, comparing quotations, monitoring orders and deliveries, and maintaining accurate purchasing records within the company's ERP system.

This role requires strong communication skills, excellent attention to detail, and the ability to manage multiple purchasing activities in a fast-paced environment. Candidates with previous experience in marine purchasing or the shipping industry will have an advantage, although applicants from other purchasing backgrounds who demonstrate strong adaptability and learning capabilities are also encouraged to apply.

Job Details:

  • Work Set-up: Work-from-Home
  • Schedule: Monday to Friday | 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM Netherlands Time | 3:00 PM to 12:00 AM Manila Time
  • Holidays: PH Holidays

Key Responsibilities:

  • Process incoming requests for quotations (RFQs) and source spare parts, equipment, and materials based on purchasing requirements.
  • Request, review, and compare supplier quotations, considering pricing, availability, specifications, and delivery lead times.
  • Communicate with local and international suppliers to obtain quotations, clarify requirements, and follow up on outstanding requests.
  • Coordinate and monitor purchasing orders, ensuring timely processing, order expediting, and delivery tracking.
  • Proactively follow up with suppliers regarding order status, delivery schedules, and potential delays.
  • Maintain accurate and up-to-date purchasing information, supplier records, product details, and transaction data within the company's ERP system.
  • Ensure accuracy and completeness when entering purchasing information, updating records, and processing documentation.
  • Coordinate closely with the sales and purchasing teams to support daily purchasing requirements and resolve supplier or order-related concerns.
  • Manage multiple RFQs, supplier communications, and purchasing activities simultaneously while maintaining accuracy and meeting deadlines.
  • Identify and promptly communicate discrepancies, order delays, or other purchasing-related issues to the appropriate team members.
  • Learn and effectively utilize the company's purchasing systems, internal procedures, and operational workflows.

Required Qualifications:

  • At least 2 years of relevant experience in purchasing, operational procurement, buying, or a similar role involving supplier coordination and purchasing administration.
  • Hands-on experience processing RFQs, requesting and comparing supplier quotations, and following up on purchase orders or deliveries.
  • Strong written and verbal English communication skills, with the ability to communicate professionally with international suppliers and colleagues.
  • Excellent organizational, administrative, and time management skills.
  • Strong attention to detail, particularly when handling product information, quotations, specifications, and data entry.
  • Ability to manage multiple tasks and competing priorities while maintaining a high level of accuracy.
  • Proficiency in using computers and business applications, with the ability to learn new ERP systems and purchasing software quickly.
  • Strong problem-solving skills, adaptability, and the ability to work effectively in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment.
  • Ability to work independently in a remote setup while maintaining effective communication and coordination with the team.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Previous purchasing experience in the marine, maritime, or shipping industry, particularly involving marine spare parts and vessel-related supplies.
  • Familiarity with purchasing operations in engineering, industrial equipment, technical supplies, or spare parts environments.
  • Experience working with ERP or purchasing management systems.
  • Familiarity with technical product descriptions, part numbers, supplier catalogs, and equipment specifications.
  • Experience coordinating with international suppliers and supporting geographically distributed teams.

Description

CapsLock is a global IT marketing company that pioneers unique, scalable customer acquisition solutions for B2C clients. We solve complex sales challenges across a wide range of industries, primarily for large North American partners. By integrating our expertise in Digital Marketing, IT, Design, AI-driven analytics, proprietary MarTech, and sales consulting, we deliver powerful, data-informed customer acquisition solutions.

At CapsLock, people, technology, and forward-thinking innovation lie at the heart of everything we do. Our diverse, global team, fluent in over 10 languages, thrives on open collaboration and the exchange of new ideas, pushing boundaries to ensure our clients' success.

Role overview

We're looking for a Marketing Design Team Lead who is equal parts creative leader, marketer, and AI geek, someone who knows how to achieve business goals through visuals that actually sell.

You will take a team of 3 AI-driven Creative Designers and scale it to 6. The team produces static ad creatives, photorealistic AI visuals for performance campaigns across paid media channels, and source assets for our video production pipeline.

Your job is to build the company's visual creative engine. Whatever the starting point- a brief, a hypothesis, a raw idea - it leaves the team as a creative that performs.

You'll work closely with Creative Producers, Marketers, Copywriters, Media Buyers, and the Video Editing team, and partner with our Generative AI Pipeline Engineer on tooling and workflows.

What you will work on

  • Lead, mentor, and scale a team of 3 to 6 AI-driven Creative Designers - grow people, not just output;
  • Own the production flow: task distribution, capacity planning, and strict QC - production-grade, not demo-grade;
  • Drive creative direction: concepts, hooks, and visual angles that stop the scroll and convert;
  • Generate ideas yourself and push the team beyond safe iterations - informed by visual trends and competitor creatives;
  • Own the creative testing loop: build a database of winners, analyze failures, turn performance data into next iterations;
  • Track new AI models and tools; be the company's go-to expert on what's creatively possible with AI, staying hands-on in the tools;
  • Run regular R&D and build prompt and style libraries that keep quality consistent as the team grows;
  • Stay hands-on: jump into the tools (Figma, Adobe Suite, AI platforms) when needed to unblock the team, take on the most complex creatives, or test new approaches;
  • Partner with the Generative AI Pipeline Engineer to turn the team's creative needs into pipelines, presets, and automation;
  • Work tightly with Creative Producers, Marketers, Media Buyers, and Video Editors: align on strategy, negotiate deadlines, solve bottlenecks.

Requirements

Your must-haves

You don't need to meet every single requirement. If you're excellent in most of these areas and can show shipped work, we'd love to hear from you.

  • 5+ years of Leadership Experience: You have successfully managed creative/design teams in digital marketing. (This is not a role for a senior designer looking for their first management gig);
  • Mature Leader & Problem Solver: You build clear processes, guide your team, gracefully resolve conflicts, remain highly proactive, and stay completely open to new ideas and approaches;
  • Strong Project Manager: You drive every project cleanly to the finish line. You guarantee top-tier quality, maintain absolute order, and hit strict deadlines without excuses;
  • Strong Visual Craft: composition, lighting, color, typography, anatomy. You can articulate exactly why a creative works or doesn't;
  • Design Toolstack: proficiency in Figma and Adobe Creative Suite; comfortable connecting AI outputs with traditional design pipelines;
  • AI Geek: far beyond basic prompting. You track every new model release and can't wait to test how it could level up ad creatives. Hands-on with modern AI image platforms (Figma Weave, Higgsfield, Magnific, Runway, or similar), using them for creating photorealistic visuals. Able to choose the right tool for each task, as well as to catch and fix artifacts.
  • Performance Marketing DNA: solid understanding of static ad creatives (Google, Meta, and other paid channels). You know what stops the scroll, what makes a visual sell, and how creative decisions move CTR, CPA, and conversion rate;
  • Fluency in English - both spoken and written.

Nice to have

  • A strong portfolio showcasing performance marketing creatives and AI-generated photorealistic work - ideally with examples shipped under your leadership and the results they drove;
  • Experience with creatives for high-CPA verticals (home improvement, insurance, health, legal, finance, or similar);
  • Experience creating visuals for North American audiences - you know what looks native to a US consumer;
  • Understanding of how static visuals feed video production pipelines.

What we offer
